newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac to build new 100 mln stg hospital.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac to build new 100 mln stg hospital.

text.p: A consortium led by British construction group Tarmac has agreed to build a 100-million-stg hospital in the UK under the government's Private Finance Initiative (PFI) scheme, Tarmac said on Tuesday.
The new hospital, which is expected to be fully operational by 2000, will provide 400 beds and replace the old hospitals at Joyce Green and West Hill, Dartford, south east England.

"Tarmac is committed to PFI in the health sector and this contract is proof that it can work. I am confident that a number of other PFI health schemes will soon follow," said Neville Simms, Tarmac chief executive, in a statement.
The Private Finance Initiative (PFI) is a government initiative to encourage private sector involvement in major infrastructure projects.
Tarmac ServiceMaster will undertake the facilities management and United Medical Enterprises will provide support services for the new hospital.
